GOOD TO KNOW

Nothing changes until you use it. No personal information is removed unless an organisation sets a retention period for it; the new retention settings start empty.

Erasing a customer now also clears the text and attachments of their messages, not only their details. Their number stays suppressed and the audit trail is kept, as before.

Not yet proven with real accounts: the MTN and Vodacom connections were built from the operators' published documents and tested against stand-ins. One part of Vodacom Messaging's dialled-menu USSD follows a public open-source integration rather than a Vodacom document; the help guide says which.

The POPIA sections and GDPR articles shown against each check are a guide to where a control applies. Have them reviewed by your compliance adviser before relying on a report for an audit.

FOR ADMINISTRATORS

Compliance: a new Compliance page (under Security) scores your organisation against ISO 27001, SOC 2, POPIA and GDPR from your own settings: two-step sign-in, sessions, allowed networks, dormant users, the audit log, retention, masking, consent, opt-outs and more. Each finding links to where it is fixed, a person can confirm what cannot be checked automatically, and the report downloads as a PDF or a spreadsheet for your auditors.

Privacy records: name your Information Officer and deputies, and your DPO and EU representative. Keep a breach register with the GDPR 72-hour clock and a reminder before it runs out; a register of processing that starts from what you actually use; your sub-processors, with the platform's own shown beside them; and cross-border transfers, flagged when none has a legal ground.

Data-subject requests: one queue for access, correction, deletion, objection and portability requests, numbered, with the due date (30 days, one extension), identity check, assignee and outcome. Export and erase close the request they belong to. Overdue requests show on the Compliance page.

Consent: search who consented to what, by channel and purpose; record or withdraw consent with its source and evidence; export the list.

Retention: optional retention periods for inactive customers, leads and messages, beside those for recordings and transcripts. Legal holds are always respected.

SMS through the operators: an SMS channel can now send through MTN OCEP or Vodacom Messaging over their web interface, or through any operator over SMPP (with settings ready for MTN and Vodacom Messaging). Delivery receipts and replies arrive by the operator's call-backs, whose addresses are shown on the channel to paste into the operator's portal, and anything missed is caught from the operator's logs. Long messages are sent in parts; the channel shows whether an SMPP link is connected. Help has a guide for each.

USSD through Vodacom Messaging: a second USSD gateway beside Grapevine, for codes dialled on any South African network. USSD prompts can also be pushed to a handset, which Vodacom allows for financial service providers only.

FOR PLATFORM OPERATORS AND RESELLERS

Security audit: every check now also shows the POPIA sections and GDPR articles it supports, with a view and a score per framework. Three new checks: the platform's privacy officers, its sub-processors, and breach notification. The platform's sub-processors are kept on this page and shown to every organisation.

Operators usually accept SMPP connections only from known addresses: allow every server that runs the webhooks worker.

FIXES

A customer who had a consent record could not be erased. They can now."}
